newsitem.title: Turkey: Turkey's Yilmaz in coalition talks with president.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz in coalition talks with president.

text.p: Turkey's prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz held talks with President Suleyman Demirel on Sunday about the formation of a secularist government, Anatolian news agency said.
Main opposition leader Yilmaz sped out of the presidential palace without making any statement to waiting reporters.
Yilmaz has been expected to ask for presidential approval at the beginning of this week for his anti-Islamist alliance of three parties.
Yilmaz was asked by the president to find a new government after Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, the first Islamist to lead modern Turkey, resigned earlier this month.
Resignations from the Erbakan's outgoing coalition have apparently given Yilmaz a slim majority in parliament.
Anatolian said earlier that Yilmaz and his two coalition partners were close to agreement on a protocol outlining the new government's policies and the distribution of cabinet seats.
"Work on the government programme will be completed on Monday, or Tuesday at the latest," the agency said.
Under Turkish law, the president must approve a new government before it goes to a confidence vote within 10 days.
Three more MPs resigned at the weekend from a pro-Islamist alliance, further boosting Yilmaz's hopes of winning a confidence vote for his secularist partnership.
"We haven't been able to secure stability in parliament. That is why I have made this move, aimed at uniting the right," Anatolian quoted deputy Evren Bulut as saying on Saturday night.
Two more True Path deputies, Ali Gunaydin and Bahattin Yucel, quit the party on Sunday, the agency said. All three were expected to back Yilmaz at the confidence vote.
His coalition is expected to give priority to encouraging secularist education and changing the electoral laws before early elections by next spring at the latest.
